header: Date: 2027-08-02T15:00Z | Duration: 42 minutes | Attendees: Avery Coleman (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (StoneHarbor), Maya Chen (StoneHarbor), Ravi Patel (StoneHarbor)
summary: Intro/demo of Redwood hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints for StoneHarbor Media search use case. Covered API flows, Console observability, cost/latency tradeoffs, caching and batching, and next steps to run a short hosted pilot and share security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Coleman: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery from Redwood, i pulled in Priya our solutions engineer to walk through the vector match flow for search. Quick roundtable - who we got?
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: Liam here, head of search at StoneHarbor. We're redoing our site search and want to improve relevance for articles and media, mostly around freshness and entity matching.
[00:17] Maya Chen: Maya, ML eng, I'll be implementing the pipeline.
[00:20] Ravi Patel: Ravi, CTO, listening for security and infra constraints.
[00:23] Priya Nair: Great, thanks. We'll do ~30 minute walkthrough then time for Qs. Quick agenda: embeddings -> candidate retrieval -> rerank -> console & optimize -> pilot next steps.
[00:36] Avery Coleman: One note, please assume recorded, we'll drop notes in the repo after.
[00:40] Liam O'Connor: Yep fine.
[00:42] Priya Nair: Ok kicking off. So the hosted embedding endpoint is a simple POST to /v1/embeddings, you send a batch of texts, we return dense vectors. We support streaming, but embeddings are usually batch. Example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{"input": ["doc text"]}' - obviously we'll share the code snippet.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Do you accept chunking? We have long articles.
[01:08] Priya Nair: Yes you can chunk client-side and we also provide tokenization helpers in the SDKs. We recommend chunking by semantic boundaries; we also have prefix caching for repeated text, though sometimes transcripts show it as KV cash in auto transcribe (laughs).
[01:26] Ravi Patel: How do you handle PII retention?
[01:29] Avery Coleman: Hosted mode stores embeddings transiently for 30 days by default unless you opt out; for strict retention you'd use Redwood Private or Dedicated. We'll attach the SOC2 + compliance pack.
[01:38] Priya Nair: Moving to retrieval: typical flow is vector search via ANN index (we integrate easily with Pinecone/FAISS/Weaviate or you can host indices). You get N candidates, then hit our rerank endpoint to run a cross-encoder or LM-based reranker that looks at full query + doc text.
[01:56] Liam O'Connor: Is rerank a separate API call? We want to limit extra hops.
[02:00] Priya Nair: Good question. It is a separate endpoint (/v1/rerank) so you do retrieval then rerank for top-K. We optimize for network round trips with batching and inline scoring options. For very tight latency needs we recommend caching top-K candidates or using an on-host lightweight rerank model.
[02:20] Maya Chen: What kind of latency numbers should we expect?
[02:23] Priya Nair: For hosted with our default rerank model: 95th percentile around 120-250ms for a top-5 rerank on a 1k token combined context. Embedding call depends on batch size but typically 30-80ms per 1k text items when batched. These are rough — we'll run pilot numbers on your dataset.
[02:44] Ravi Patel: Any deterministic SLAs for hosted?
[02:46] Avery Coleman: Hosted has best-effort with usage tiers; SLA-backed latency and uptime are part of Redwood Dedicated and Private tiers. But we do offer reserved capacity bursts for hosted customers if predictability is needed.
[03:00] Priya Nair: I'll show the Console now. Opening per-route dashboard — you can see per-model token breakdown, latency waterfall, and cost by token. Optimize tab will surface suggestions like increase batch size to 16 for your QPS to reduce cost by ~18%, or enable KV caching for frequently repeated prefixes.
[03:22] Maya Chen: Is that Optimize automated or manual?
[03:24] Priya Nair: It's recommendations with suggested config changes. You can apply them automatically for non-breaking changes or run A/B tests via the rollout feature.
[03:33] Liam O'Connor: About cost — we're trying to hit sub-$0.05 per search average. Is that realistic?
[03:38] Avery Coleman: Depends on model choices and rerank depth. Using a smaller embedding model + lightweight reranker can get you there. Optimize will simulate estimated cost per config for your QPS. We'll include a pricing worksheet illustrating tradeoffs.
[03:52] Ravi Patel: Security dive: how does auth work and can we integrate SAML SSO?
[03:56] Avery Coleman: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC for Console; API keys for service integrations. For hosted we offer customer-managed keys integration with KMS options for encryption at rest. Audit logs are available in the Console and can be exported.
[04:10] Priya Nair: Also mention RBAC for team roles.
[04:13] Maya Chen: For the pilot, will we need to provide infra changes? We prefer not to touch infra.
[04:18] Priya Nair: Hosted pilot requires only dataset upload and API calls, no infra changes. If you later choose Private or Dedicated we do a VPC peering or on-prem install with more infra work.
[04:28] Liam O'Connor: Can you do canonical examples of rerank scoring? I want to see the diff between embedding-only cosine vs rerank with the cross-encoder.
[04:34] Priya Nair: Yes — we'll run a small ab experiment: recall @K for ANN candidates vs rerank precision uplift. In our benchmarks rerank typically gives a 12-30% lift in click-through metrics for document-heavy corpora. We'll share the benchmark script and results.
[04:52] Ravi Patel: Any concerns about model hallucinations when reranking?
[04:55] Priya Nair: Reranker is constrained and uses the doc text, but you should still include guardrails and thresholds. Console offers anomaly detection on output quality and rollback on regression.
[05:08] Avery Coleman: Quick live demo — Priya, do you want to run the hosted flow against a sample dataset?
[05:12] Priya Nair: Sure. I'm switching to the Console. Loading the demo index... there might be a small lag.
[05:30] [screen share noise] Priya Nair: Ok here's a sample query: 'best practices for podcast metadata ingestion' — hitting /v1/embeddings for the query, retrieving top 50 with our ANN connector, then POST to /v1/rerank for top-5.
[05:50] Maya Chen: I see the request bodies. Are you sending the full doc text to rerank?
[05:54] Priya Nair: We send the snippet or the canonical doc depending on your config; you can pass the top-K doc id and we fetch content if you prefer server-side fetch. We do respect data residency flags.
[06:06] Liam O'Connor: The response time looked decent on the demo. Can we throttle concurrency? We have bursty traffic.
[06:12] Priya Nair: Yes — throttle and autoscale policies are configurable. Hosted autoscaling handles bursts, Dedicated gives guaranteed throughput. You can also set per-route rate limits.
[06:24] Maya Chen: About index updates — we ingest daily, sometimes hourly. Does that invalidate caches?
[06:29] Priya Nair: Cache keys use doc fingerprinting so only changed docs evict. For prefix KV cache, if you have partial updates we may reindex deltas.
[06:42] Ravi Patel: Can we restrict which models are accessible to our team in Console?
[06:46] Avery Coleman: Yes, RBAC + model allowlists are supported. You can pin model versions for routes to ensure reproducible outputs.
[06:55] Priya Nair: Back to costs — here's the Optimize suggestion table. For your QPS of ~40 peak: batch size 8 embeddings, top-K rerank 5, estimated per-search cost $0.041 with these picks. Switching to a quantized model for rerank reduces to $0.032 but adds ~25ms latency.
[07:18] Maya Chen: That latency tradeoff might be acceptable. Is quantization supported on hosted?
[07:22] Priya Nair: Yes, we expose quantized variants of some models in hosted. For strict accuracy-sensitive flows we recommend testing against your eval set.
[07:33] Liam O'Connor: On evals — can we integrate our offline relevance labels?
[07:36] Priya Nair: Absolutely. Console has an evals page where you upload labeled pairs; it will run A/Bs and surface regressions tied to prompts and model changes.
[07:46] Ravi Patel: Any compliance packages for media companies? We may need contract clauses about content takedown and DMCA handling.
[07:53] Avery Coleman: We'll loop legal in — we have enterprise add-ons and can include clauses around content retention and takedown processes.
[08:02] Priya Nair: Ok switching to technical details — for the rerank we use an optimized cross-encoder path that leverages continuous batching on the GPU runtime; kernel selection adapts to sequence length. That bit sometimes shows up in our notes as 'kernel selection thingy' — transcripts are messy.
[08:21] Maya Chen: How about shard locality and region routing? We have users in EU and NA.
[08:25] Priya Nair: Region-based routing is policy-driven. Hosted will route to nearest region; Dedicated/Private supports strict residency. Also we can do smart routing by policy so EU queries stay in EU.
[08:36] Liam O'Connor: For the pilot, what data do you need from us?
[08:40] Priya Nair: A sample of 50k to 100k documents, expected QPS profile, and a small labeled set for evaluation. Also any compliance requirements for the storage or key management.
[08:51] Maya Chen: We'll need to anonymize some fields.
[08:53] Priya Nair: Noted — we can also run with redacted payloads if needed.
[08:57] [09:00] Avery Coleman: Quick Q from Liam: competitors — you mentioned Anthropic earlier, how are we different on cost control?
[09:06] Priya Nair: We focus on inference economics: Optimize suggestions, configurable batching, quantized model variants, and transparent per-token cost breakdown in Console. That often results in lower total cost for production workloads.
[09:19] Liam O'Connor: Any known limitations?
[09:21] Priya Nair: Very long rerank contexts can spike latency; also if you need deterministic outputs we recommend pinning model versions. Hosted model pool changes can cause slightly different outputs over time unless pinned.
[09:33] Maya Chen: For the rerank endpoint, do you support function/tool calling or structured output?
[09:37] Priya Nair: Rerank is scoring-focused, but our generation endpoints support structured output and tool calls. You can combine them in a pipeline.
[09:45] Ravi Patel: Let's talk timeline. If we start next week, how long to pilot?
[09:50] Avery Coleman: 2-3 week pilot typical: onboarding + initial index + evaluation. Priya will run the benchmark and we'll reconvene with results.
[09:58] Priya Nair: Now I'll show the traces — Console has per-request tracing; you can see token-level latencies and where time is spent (embedding, ANN lookup, rerank). This helps tune batch sizes.
[10:14] Liam O'Connor: That trace view looks useful. Can we export traces to our observability stack?
[10:18] Priya Nair: Yes, we support exports to Datadog/Prometheus and webhook sinks.
[10:23] Maya Chen: Any gotchas around tokenization differences? We use a different tokenizer in our pipeline.
[10:28] Priya Nair: Tokenization mismatch can affect embedding semantics; we recommend using our SDK tokenizers or ensuring parity. We can run a quick tokenization parity test in the pilot.
[10:40] [10:55] Avery Coleman: Wrapping to questions and next steps in a second. Quick note on pricing doc — I'll share examples for the different model combos.
[11:02] Liam O'Connor: If we move to Dedicated later, how does migration look?
[11:06] Priya Nair: There's a lift-and-shift option; you can keep same API surface and just point routes to Dedicated. We'll help migrate index/backfills and validate outputs.
[11:16] Maya Chen: Are there SDKs for Java? We use a Java backend.
[11:19] Priya Nair: Yes, we have JS, Python, and Java SDKs. We'll share links.
[11:26] Ravi Patel: Anything else on compliance?
[11:29] Avery Coleman: We'll include the SOC2 cert and the KMS integration docs, plus an exportable audit log sample.
[11:36] Priya Nair: Alright final recap: pilot with 50-100k docs, Priya runs benchmark and shares results, Avery sends pricing + security docs, and schedule follow-up deep-dive with infra team next week.
[11:49] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good, thanks both.
[11:52] Maya Chen: Thanks all.
[11:54] Ravi Patel: Thanks.
[12:00] [END]
